title: Connection pooling: modes, transaction scope and the traps

videos.script: Every connection to PostgreSQL is a process on the server, and the server allows a hundred. The hundred and first client is turned away. {{refused}} A pooler sits in between: many clients on one side, a few busy connections on the other. You install PgBouncer and run your own, on port 6433. {{pgbouncer}} The same hundred and twenty clients go through twenty connections, and none of them fails. {{twenty}} Then the trap. One client sets a timeout and leaves. The next client, which set nothing, is cancelled by it. {{leak}} SET LOCAL keeps a setting inside its transaction. {{local}} And session mode, which leaks nothing, and makes everybody else wait for a whole session. {{session}}
